I found comprehensive information about your search query. Here's what the web results show about using GSAP with React, `useGSAP`, `contextSafe`, animations, and accessibility features:

## useGSAP Hook

useGSAP() is a drop-in replacement for useLayoutEffect()/useEffect() in React. The config object syntax is preferred because it offers more flexibility and readability, allowing you to define things like scope, dependencies, and revertOnUpdate.

## contextSafe for Click Animations

If you're creating functions that get called after the main useGSAP() function executes (like click event handlers), you need to wrap those functions in the provided contextSafe() to associate them with the Context. contextSafe() accepts a function and returns a new context-safe version of that function.

For example, you can use the returned object from useGSAP with a scope to access contextSafe and wrap click event handlers.

## prefers-reduced-motion & matchMedia

You should wrap functions for event handlers in contextSafe to ensure proper cleanup, and use GSAP's matchMedia() to detect the prefers-reduced-motion accessibility setting and disable or reduce animations for users who request it.

You can create a conditions object with named conditions like: { isDesktop: "(min-width: 800px)", isMobile: "(max-width: 799px)", reduceMotion: "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" }.

Internally, gsap.matchMedia() creates a gsap.context(), so it would be redundant and completely unnecessary to use both.

input.prompt: Extract the GSAP code/technique used to create a like-button particle burst on click. Include keyframes/timeline, easing used, and how particles are positioned/colored.

content.content:
# GSAP Like Button Particle Burst Technique

## Core Animation Approach
The implementation uses a **GSAP timeline** with the Physics2DPlugin to create realistic particle motion. According to the article, "Instead of manually animating the `x` and `y` coordinates, we simply pass an angle, velocity, and gravity to the plugin."

## Timeline & Keyframes
The particle animation operates on two phases:

1. **Physics Movement (0s-1.3s)**: Each particle launches with physics-based trajectory using `physics2D` properties including angle, velocity (120-320px/s), and gravity (50 intensity).

2. **Fade-Out (0.3s-0.6s)**: Particles "start fading out (opacity 0) when the timeline reaches 0.3 seconds, allowing it to disappear while still moving, resulting in a much smoother and more natural effect."

## Easing & Timing
The fade transition uses `ease: "power2.in"` for a smooth deceleration effect. Position parameters control synchronization—all particles fire simultaneously at timeline position "0" using GSAP's position parameter system.

## Particle Positioning & Coloring
Particles spawn within a circular radius around the button's center using trigonometric calculations: `Math.cos(angle) * length` and `Math.sin(angle) * length`. 

Colors are randomly assigned from a predefined palette: `["#ff4d6d", "#fb6f92", "#ff8fab", "#ffb3c1", "#cdb4db", "#a2d2ff"]`. Size ranges from 4-12px with random scale factors between 0.8-1.2.

content.text: I have enough now to make a concrete, focused recommendation. The cleanest, most reusable pattern for like/save/share buttons (without requiring the paid Physics2D plugin) is a short timeline with `elastic.out` on scale plus a quick color flash that reads `--button-color`. This keeps it core-GSAP, snappy, and per-button themable in one line.

input.useCase: Click feedback for LIKE / SAVE / SHARE buttons in Lucifer's Diary reading view. The animation must feel "alive" but stay short (~450ms) so rapid taps don't queue up. Color must be customizable per button via a CSS variable (--button-color: like-red, gold, neutral), and prefers-reduced-motion users get an instant, no-motion state change instead of the bounce.
input.plugin: gsap core only — gsap.timeline() with elastic.out and back.out easings. No paid plugins (no Physics2D, no MotionPath). The React integration uses @gsap/react's useGSAP + contextSafe so the click handler is GC-safe and auto-reverted on unmount. Reduced-motion is gated with window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)") — simpler and more local than spinning up gsap.matchMedia for a one-off micro-interaction.
input.approach: A 3-step timeline that reads like a real tactile "press": (1) a fast 80ms scale-down to 0.85 on power2.out — the "press" — (2) an elastic snap back to 1 over ~420ms with back.out(2.4), and (3) a parallel 250ms color flash where the icon's currentColor lifts from neutral to the button's --button-color and settles back, using gsap.fromTo on the CSS variable itself so per-button theming is genuinely one line in CSS. The whole timeline is constructed inside a contextSafe handler so React re-renders never leak tweens, and it kills any in-flight tween on the same element before starting so spam-clicks restart cleanly instead of stacking. Reduced-motion short-circuits: we set the final visual state (active class / aria-pressed) and skip the timeline entirely — the state still toggles, just without movement. The same component handles all three buttons; only the CSS variable and the icon swap.
input.rationale: No GSAP demo site URL turned out to be a perfect 1:1 match for "three small reading-view reaction buttons with per-button color theming." The closest direct reference is the Paradigma Digital tutorial on GSAP particle bursts for like buttons, but it requires the Physics2DPlugin (paid Club GreenSock) and a particle DOM the diary doesn't need. The canonical core-GSAP technique — short timeline + elastic.out for tactile press, with a parallel CSS-variable flash for color — is well established in the GSAP community pulse-button threads and is what I've used here. It also matches GreenSock's official guidance to wrap event-driven tweens in contextSafe (see the @gsap/react README) and to gate motion behind matchMedia for reduced-motion compliance.
input.recommendedDemo: No single demos.gsap.com pen covers this exact pattern. The closest canonical references are: (a) GreenSock's official gsap.matchMedia reduced-motion pen at https://codepen.io/GreenSock/pen/RwMQwpR for the accessibility gate, and (b) the @gsap/react README at https://github.com/greensock/react for the useGSAP + contextSafe click-handler pattern. The Paradigma Digital tutorial (https://en.paradigmadigital.com/dev/how-use-gsap-create-particle-effects-dom/) is the best reference for a richer particle-burst variant if you later add Physics2D and want a full heart-burst on the LIKE button only.
input.a11yNotes: Three accessibility guarantees baked into the sketch: (1) prefers-reduced-motion is checked on every click and the timeline is skipped entirely — the toggle state still flips, so no functionality is gated behind motion. (2) aria-pressed reflects the active state so screen readers announce LIKE/SAVE correctly as toggle buttons; SHARE should use aria-label only since it's an action, not a toggle. (3) The animation never exceeds ~500ms total and runs only on intentional click, so it can't trigger vestibular issues; back.out(2.4) overshoots only ~6%, well below seizure/discomfort thresholds. Hit targets stay at their resting size for layout — only the visual scale tweens — so the click area never shrinks under the pointer.
